policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect (UAF-adjacent resource-teardown-ordering regression) enumerated in cpp-safety's blocking contract
summary: gw_mgmt_pool_.reset() was placed mirroring gateway_route_store_.reset(), which was wrong for this resource: unlike that store (read only by gRPC handler threads already drained by mgmt_server_->Shutdown()), gw_mgmt_pool_ is also read by forward_gateway_pending()'s detached, untracked threads (#3279). The mirrored placement freed the pool's channels/stubs up to ~60s+ earlier than the pre-4.3 code ever did (never explicitly reset in stop() at all), widening #3279's existing UAF window.
trigger: stop() executing while >=1 forward_gateway_pending() detached thread is still in its retry/backoff loop

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: moved gw_mgmt_pool_.reset()/set_known_gateway_clusters(nullptr) to immediately before pg_pool_.reset() — the latest practical point in stop(), restoring parity with pre-4.3 timing. Re-verified independently by security-guardian and cpp-safety in a dedicated Gate 8 re-review pass; cpp-safety explicitly retracted its own earlier (incorrect) 'essentially the same point' characterization after re-tracing stop()'s full body.

classification_rationale: required per the six-item required-doc list, item 2 (docs/user-manual/ section for a new CLI flag)
summary: --gateway-cluster-addr (and the pre-existing --gateway-command-addr) is absent from the 'Server CLI Flags' reference table. Consistent with every prior WS-4 slice, which never touched docs/user-manual/ for this workstream (ADR-2002 + the delivery matrix have been the sole doc surface) — judged non-blocking against that precedent.
trigger: new CLI flag shipped with no docs/user-manual/ table row

summary: Independently re-raised by enterprise-readiness at Gate 6 (same underlying gap, plus noting --gateway-command-addr was already missing pre-existing). Per enterprise-readiness's own recommendation (no current customer-facing/pilot path to multi-cluster gateway deployment yet), filed as a follow-up rather than fixed in this PR: https://github.com/Tr3kkR/Yuzu/issues/4667
The #3279 tracked-pointer-reach comment (enumerating what forward_gateway_pending's detached thread touches) was not updated to name the new Stub* resolved from gw_mgmt_pool_.
trigger: new raw-pointer capture added to an already-tracked untracked-thread reach set with no comment update

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: extended the #3279 comment block to name the new Stub* capture and cross-reference the stop()-ordering fix. Re-verified accurate by cpp-safety's Gate 8 re-review.

The response agent-id mismatch guard and not_connected classification were inline in forward_gateway_pending's detached-thread lambda, with no fake ManagementService test harness in the codebase to exercise them.
trigger: new security-relevant guard shipped with no direct unit test, though a pure-function extraction seam was available

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: extracted classify_gateway_forward_response (gateway_mgmt_stub_pool.hpp) as a pure function, with 6 new unit tests covering every outcome including the security-critical mismatch-checked-first property. Re-verified by security-guardian and cpp-safety Gate 8 passes (confirmed the extraction preserves exact behavioral parity and the mismatch check fires unconditionally before any content inspection).

The stream_responses/3 fix (threading the real command_id through a command_error-derived response) had no direct eunit test — only the pre-existing 321-test suite staying green, which proves no regression but not that the fix works.
trigger: behavioral fix shipped with only negative (suite-stays-green) test evidence, no positive assertion

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: added send_command_stamps_real_command_id_on_not_connected_error_test, mocking the fan-out and outgoing stream send. Independently re-verified false-green-safe by gateway-erlang's Gate 8 re-review (traced that the test would have failed against the pre-fix hardcoded <<>>).

GatewayMgmtStubPool::resolve()'s present-but-empty std::optional<std::string>("") cluster_id path was untested (only nullopt and non-empty strings covered) — same code path as nullopt per the guard condition, low value but a real gap.
trigger: an equivalence class of the resolution rule left unasserted

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: added a dedicated test asserting present-empty resolves identically to nullopt in both single- and multi-cluster mode.

unmapped_cluster_seen (the CONNECTED-time early-warning metric outcome) was not pre-seeded in the boot-time metrics-seed loop, breaking absent-vs-zero for exactly the signal designed to warn an operator early.
trigger: boot-time seed loop omitted one real status value on a pre-seeded metric family

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: added the seed under the same gate condition ('unknown' in the label set) as the existing seeding. Re-verified correct by sre's Gate 8 re-review.

A hardcoded "unknown" string literal was used instead of the shared kUnknownGatewayClusterLabel constant (gateway_mgmt_stub_pool.hpp) — values happened to match but would silently desync if the constant ever changed.
trigger: a metric label value duplicated as a literal instead of referencing the single source of truth

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: now uses yuzu::server::kUnknownGatewayClusterLabel. Re-verified by sre's Gate 8 re-review.
unmapped_clusters_warned_ (log-dedup set) was unbounded in entry count — a session cycling through many distinct malformed/misconfigured cluster_id values grew it indefinitely.
trigger: a session (or several) announcing many distinct unmapped cluster_id values over process lifetime

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344 (kMaxUnmappedClustersWarned=256 cap). This first fix bounded memory correctly but was ITSELF found by unhappy-path (Gate 4, finding UP-6) to let LOGGING degrade to unbounded past the cap — see ws443-uphappy-log-flood-past-cap for the superseding fix in ea67d19c5. sre's Gate 8 re-review of the FIRST fix (before UP-6 was found) confirmed the memory-bounding property correct; the log-volume gap was a distinct, later-discovered issue in the same mechanism.

No alert rule existed for the agent_mismatch outcome (a potential response-forgery signal) despite the file's own established 'any occurrence is actionable' precedent (YuzuGatewayMgmtAuthRejected) applying to this class, distinct from unknown_cluster's legitimately-deferred 'needs real fleet baseline' class.
trigger: a new potential-forgery failure signal shipped with a metric but no alert

summary: Fixed in 08d6bd344: added YuzuGatewayResponseAgentMismatch (increase(...)>0, no for:, severity warning, matching YuzuGatewayMgmtAuthRejected's structure). Re-verified by sre's Gate 8 re-review, including confirming severity:warning (not critical) is internally consistent with the file's own precedent for a comparable signal. Independently confirmed unhappy-path Gate 4's UP-5 (which asked for exactly this alert) was already satisfied by this fix.

The new eunit test's meck:unload calls were not wrapped in try/after — an assertion failure mid-test would leave yuzu_gw_router/grpcbox_stream mecked for the rest of the eunit run, which a later module (yuzu_gw_registry_multinode_tests, calling the real yuzu_gw_router:send_command/3) would silently hit.
trigger: an assertion failure inside this specific test, combined with a later test in the same eunit run calling the real mocked module

summary: Fixed in 583005173: wrapped the test body in try/after so meck:unload always runs. Verified: rebar3 eunit 322/322, dialyzer clean.

YuzuGatewayResponseAgentMismatch's summary said 'forwarded a response for an unrequested agent' but the guard actually REFUSES the mismatched response — an operator skimming only the summary could misread a rejection as an applied forgery.
trigger: wording imprecision in a new alert's summary annotation

summary: Fixed in 583005173: reworded to 'Gateway rejected a response for an unrequested agent'.

forward_gateway_pending's early return when gw_mgmt_pool_ is null/empty drained gw_pending_ unconditionally first, then returned with zero log and zero metric — including when gateway forwarding IS configured but unusable (credential construction failed at boot), a real fleet-wide silent command-loss case.
trigger: gateway forwarding configured but build_gateway_command_credentials() fails at boot

summary: Fixed in ea67d19c5: distinguishes unconfigured (stays silent, correct) from configured-but-unusable (now logs + counts once per drain). Full build clean, targeted suites green (390 assertions); full suite run in progress at commit time, confirmed green before push.

The prior round's unmapped_clusters_warned_ cap fix (ws443-sre-unbounded-unmapped-clusters-set) correctly bounded memory but let LOGGING degrade to unbounded: past the cap, first_warning was recomputed as !contains(id) every time for any new distinct id, which is never inserted past the cap — so it re-warns on EVERY occurrence forever. A gateway peer already past mTLS+peer-pin auth but varying its announced cluster_id across reconnects could drive an unbounded per-connect WARN rate.
trigger: 256+ distinct unmapped cluster_id values seen, then a peer continuing to vary its announced value across reconnects

summary: Fixed in ea67d19c5: past the cap, per-occurrence logging is suppressed entirely (metric still counts every occurrence); one explicit transition warning fires when the cap is first reached. Supersedes the disposition of ws443-sre-unbounded-unmapped-clusters-set's original fix, which addressed memory but not log volume.

No code path verifies a configured --gateway-cluster-addr host:port is actually the claimed cluster — a reasonable, but previously undocumented, trust boundary (mTLS authenticates core's own identity outward, not the peer's claimed identity back).
trigger: operator misconfiguration or stale DNS pointing a cluster_id at the wrong peer

summary: Fixed in ea67d19c5: added an explicit TRUST BOUNDARY section to gateway_mgmt_stub_pool.hpp's file header.

yuzu_server_gateway_forward_total's describe() HELP text enumerated 7 status values but an 8th real, correctly-pre-seeded value (unmapped_cluster_seen, a connect-time signal sharing the metric name) was never mentioned in the HELP text itself.
trigger: an operator reading only the metric's self-description to enumerate legal status values

summary: Fixed in ea67d19c5: extended the HELP text to name unmapped_cluster_seen and explain its distinct (connect-time, not dispatch-time) semantics.
